title: Nani Goes Pan-World: The Paradise Will Release in Nine Languages — Including Spanish
excerpt: Srikanth Odela's Dasara reunion just unveiled a moustache-twirling Raghav Juyal as villain Vikram Maalik — and a global rollout aimed at audiences far beyond the Telugu-Tamil corridor.
body:
Nine languages. Read that again — *nine*. When **Nani** unveiled the new poster for **The Paradise**, the eye-catcher wasn't the brooding hero or the apocalyptic landscape behind him. It was the fine print: Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Bengali, English, and — wait for it — **Spanish**. The Natural Star isn't going pan-India anymore. He's going pan-*world*, and he's bringing a Spanish dub to do it.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=sH5GXIlEe-8</youtube>

This is a long way from the boy-next-door who charmed his way through *Jersey* and *Hi Nanna*. Reuniting with **Srikanth Odela** — the director who turned *Dasara* into a coal-dust-and-blood sensation — Nani has remade himself as **Jadal**, a man clawing up from the bottom of Jadal Zamana, hungry for identity, recognition, and a name people fear. The first single, *Aaya Sher*, scored by the inescapable **Anirudh Ravichander**, already told you the register: raw, rustic, feral. This is Nani with the charm sanded off and the menace dialed up.

And then, last week, the makers handed us the villain — and what a reveal it was.

At 6:03 PM, precisely teased to the minute, **Raghav Juyal** arrived as **Vikram Maalik**, and the internet did a double-take. Yes, *that* Raghav Juyal — the dancer, the slo-mo king, the affable host. Here he is unrecognizable: handlebar moustache, draped in gold, eyes lit with something genuinely unsettling, the self-appointed *Chota Maalik* of a city he believes belongs to him.

> "Aankhon mein shaitaanik. Shehar mera taalik. Naam mera khaufik." — Srikanth Odela, introducing Vikram Maalik

It's pulpy, it's swaggering, and it works. The character video — set to *Chota Maalik*, another Anirudh banger — plays like a gauntlet thrown at Nani's feet. The chemistry teased between hero and antagonist, the promise of a rivalry built on contempt, is exactly the combustible fuel a mass actioner runs on. For Juyal, who has been quietly stacking interesting choices, this is the swing-for-the-fences villain turn that could reclassify him entirely. On this evidence, he's never been better.

The ensemble is stacked with texture: veteran **Mohan Babu** as Shikanja Malik, **Kayadu Lohar** as the female lead, with Sonali Kulkarni, Tanikella Bharani, Sampoornesh Babu, and Eeshwari Rao rounding it out. Behind the camera, Odela has assembled a genuine A-team — cinematographer **Sathyan Sooryan** (the eye behind *Jailer*), editor Navin Nooli, production designer Avinash Kolla, with colour grading by Red Chillies. This is not a film cutting corners.

There is, however, a wrinkle. **The Paradise has moved.** Originally circled for a March 2026 release, the film has now skipped to **August 21, 2026**, a shift widely read as the *Dhurandhar* effect rippling through an overcrowded calendar. The new date is no retreat — it parks Nani squarely in the lucrative Independence Day window, prime real estate for a film with this much scale and this loud a roar. Better a strong solo run in August than a bruising March clash.

**The diaspora angle here is almost too on-the-nose.** A nine-language release with a dedicated Spanish track is a film studio openly courting audiences far beyond the usual Telugu-Tamil corridors of New Jersey and the Bay Area. For NRIs in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia, a Nani film releasing in English *and* Spanish signals theatrical availability across far more markets than a typical Tollywood title ever gets — and it's a quiet bet that Odela's gritty, universal underdog story can travel the way *RRR* proved Indian spectacle could. Expect a wide overseas footprint when August lands; the Spanish dub is a statement of intent aimed squarely at Latin America and the US Hispanic market.

Here's the take: *Dasara* proved the Nani-Odela pairing could conjure something elemental out of mud and rage. *The Paradise* is them doing it again, but bigger, louder, and pointed at the entire globe. The Juyal reveal alone moved this from "watch later" to "must-watch." If the film delivers on the promise of its assets, August 21 won't just be a Telugu release — it'll be a worldwide event with a moustache-twirling villain you won't be able to look away from.
